clue.text: Luxury extension can perhaps ruin housing

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the word that comes before it is only one possible arrangement of its letters
a word that is housing something holds it inside, so the ruin word wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: EXT is the standard abbreviation for a telephone extension
to ravage is to ruin or lay waste
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A home extension is an indulgence that might wreck the house it is built onto.
explanation.walkthrough: EXT is followed by RAVAGE, which holds ANC, a reshuffle of CAN, giving EXTRAVAGANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Extravagance is lavish spending on comforts beyond need, which is what luxury means as a noun.

clue.text: Elizabeth knights old boy, long having earned top honour

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: E is the initial of Elizabeth, as on the royal cypher EIIR
N is the chess notation for a knight, so two knights are NN
OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil
L is the abbreviation for long, as in clothing sizes
the first letter of earned

explanation.surface: The Queen dubs a former public schoolboy who has spent years earning the highest award.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Elizabeth knights' as the definition, but the answer is a verb meaning honour, at the very end; Elizabeth only supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the peerage or dignify them, a formal way of conferring honour on a person.

clue.text: Be grateful husband's abandoned cap and jumper from the 1970s

indicators.note: the husband has abandoned the phrase before it, meaning his letter walks out of that word

blocks.note: to thank someone is to show you are grateful
H is the abbreviation for husband
a cap or lid is a top

explanation.surface: A thankful man walks out leaving behind his hat and a retro sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; a tank top is a sleeveless knitted one, hugely fashionable in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless pullover worn over a shirt, a garment strongly associated with seventies fashion.

clue.text: Organising fishing, gutted after young salmon head off

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, so a letter from the interior of the word goes
with its head off, the word loses its first letter
'after' places the fishing part behind the salmon part

blocks.note: a parr is a young salmon in its first freshwater stage
angling is fishing with a rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler arranges a trip, cleaning the catch after decapitating a small salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: PARR minus its head is ARR, and ANGLING with its inner L taken out is ANGING; the salmon part comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging means putting things in order or making plans for an event, the same as organising.

clue.text: Top grade carbon copy's acquired quickly

indicators.note: what has been acquired is taken inside, so the copy word gathers the other letters within it

blocks.note: A is the highest mark in a grading scheme
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to ape someone is to copy or imitate them

explanation.surface: A high-quality duplicate made with carbon paper has been obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon copy' looks like a single phrase, but carbon is just C and copy is APE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is a literary adverb meaning at a swift speed, so it can replace quickly.

clue.text: Rambling work emails get skipped initially

indicators.note: read as a command, 'work' tells you to work the letters over into a new shape
'initially' keeps just the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of skipped

explanation.surface: Long, wandering work emails are ignored by recipients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work emails' reads as office messages, but work is an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless describes something lacking purpose or direction, just as a rambling speech wanders without a clear point.

clue.text: Museum manager's almost rude about schedule

indicators.note: 'almost' means not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped
turned about, the schedule word faces the other way

blocks.note: curt means rudely brief
a rota is a schedule of duties taken in turn

explanation.surface: The person running the museum is nearly rude when discussing the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means 'concerning', but here it turns the schedule word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the keeper in charge of a museum or gallery collection, responsible for its exhibits.

clue.text: Now and then, during poetic evening, gets extremely mushy about love

indicators.note: what happens during the evening sits inside it, so those letters go within the evening word
'about' puts the mushy word around the love letter

blocks.note: very and extremely both intensify
soft means sentimental, mushy
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
e'en is the poetic contraction of evening

explanation.surface: On a romantic poetry evening, someone turns very sentimental about love.
explanation.walkthrough: E'en is an old poetic contraction; love as O comes from the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Every so often is an idiom meaning occasionally, at intervals, which is exactly what now and then means.

clue.text: Wine seller's very trendy having the Queen on flipping books!

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the books abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
what is in is fashionable
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A wine merchant is very fashionable, displaying books about the Queen, which annoys someone mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British oath, as in 'flipping books!', but it reverses NT to TN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner is a wine merchant, someone who deals in and sells wine as a trade.

clue.text: Nowadays on edge about lover

indicators.note: brought about means turned around, so the pair of words before it run backwards

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
re means on or concerning
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: These days someone is nervous about a romantic partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' reads as nervous, but on and edge are separate words, read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a suitor, someone romantically attracted to another person, which is one sense of lover.

clue.text: Special celebration for Socialist landlord, always pursuing end of need

indicators.note: what is pursuing something runs behind it, so the always word comes after the need letter
'end of' keeps only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: a red is a socialist
a letter is one who lets property
the last letter of need
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A left-wing landlord enjoys a special party, permanently chasing what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Landlord is not a pub keeper here but one who lets, a LETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a memorable, joyful occasion, from the saints' days printed in red on church calendars.

clue.text: Harp on about fragment found in wreck

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so the fragment word sits within the wreck word

blocks.note: a ruin is a wreck
a bit is a small fragment

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going on about a piece of debris recovered from a shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub it in is an idiom for dwelling tactlessly on someone's mistake, repeatedly reminding them, which is harping on.

clue.text: Sad when leader's taken away to be thrown out

indicators.note: its leader is the first letter, and taking it away removes that letter from the front

blocks.note: dejected means downcast, sad

explanation.surface: A party feels sad when its leader is ousted and expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ejected is to be forcibly removed from a place, expelled, the same as thrown out.

clue.text: Push church seating back to accommodate end of cortege

indicators.note: 'back' tells you to read the seating word from the back
to accommodate a guest is to take them in, so a letter is housed within the seating word
'end of' keeps only the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: pews are the benches in a church
the last letter of cortege

explanation.surface: Pews are pushed back in a church to make room for a funeral procession.
explanation.walkthrough: PEWS reversed is SWEP, with E from cortege inserted. A cortege is a funeral procession.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep something along is to push or drive it before you, as with a broom or a strong current.

clue.text: Kept back popular book

blocks.note: what is in is popular
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A popular book has been held back for later.
explanation.walkthrough: Book is the verb, as in booking a seat, not a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in reserve is set aside for later use, which is what kept back means.

clue.text: Reasons to control allowance of beer

blocks.note: to ration is to control how much each person is allowed
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: There are good grounds for limiting how much beer people get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reasons to control' wants to be one phrase; the definition stops after Reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the set of underlying grounds or logic for a decision, so it means reasons.

clue.text: Give short change in error

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, here altering the order of the letters before it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop assistant hands over too little change by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short change' reads as one shop phrase; short belongs to the letters and change signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something, an unintentional slip or error.

clue.text: On way to thrashing after Everton edges second penalty

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, first and last
'after' puts the thrashing word behind the edges of the club name
'second' picks out the letter in position two of the following word

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Everton
a rout is a heavy defeat, a thrashing
the second letter of penalty

explanation.surface: A team heads to a heavy defeat after Everton edge ahead with a second penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club; 'edges' looks like a verb about scoring but takes its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: En route is a French borrowing meaning along the way or in transit, travelling towards a place.

clue.text: With team short, reserve comes on and equalises

indicators.note: a word that is short is missing its tail, so its last letter goes
the reserve comes on after the team, so its letters are added next

blocks.note: a squad is a team
RES is the abbreviation for reserve

explanation.surface: A side down to ten men brings on a substitute, who scores the equaliser.
explanation.definitionFit: To square a match or contest is to level the score, making the two sides even again.

clue.text: Seed diet oddly not for songbird

indicators.note: not the odd-numbered letters means keeping the even ones, positions two and four

blocks.note: a pip is a fruit seed
the second and fourth letters of diet

explanation.surface: A bird's diet of seeds is said to be strangely unsuitable for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brown songbird of open country, related to wagtails, such as the meadow pipit.

clue.text: Rep confused old lady, pocketing first insurance payment

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled, so the word before is jumbled
pocketing something puts it inside, so the old lady word holds a letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
your old lady is informal for your mother, mum in Britain
I is the Roman numeral one, the first

explanation.surface: A muddled salesman takes an elderly woman's first payment for a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium is the regular sum paid to an insurer to keep a policy in force.

clue.text: Strategy also included a group of soldiers

indicators.note: what a thing has included is inside it, so the strategy word wraps the other

blocks.note: a plan is a strategy
too means also

explanation.surface: The battle plan also involved a unit of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small military unit of a few sections, commanded by a lieutenant, a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Hard to follow abridged article from beginning to end

indicators.note: the hard word is to follow, so it comes after the article part
an abridged text is cut short, so the article loses its last letter

blocks.note: the is the definite article
rough means hard or harsh

explanation.surface: A shortened newspaper article is still difficult to read from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to follow' reads as difficult to understand, but it splits into hard and an order instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Through, as in reading a book through, means completely, covering the whole thing from start to finish.

clue.text: Act badly, losing lead in a board game

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its first letter is used
'in' places that single letter inside the acting word

blocks.note: to ham is to overact
the first letter of losing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone performs poorly after falling behind in a game played on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing lead' looks like a deletion instruction, but it supplies L to go into HAM, with A after.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a Victorian strategy game of jumping pieces across a checkered grid, the ancestor of Chinese chequers.

clue.text: Outside broadcast follows golf tournament

indicators.note: the broadcast word follows, so it goes after the tournament

blocks.note: the Open is golf's oldest major championship
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: TV coverage from location comes after a golf championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcast' is a television term for filming on location, but the definition is Outside alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outdoors rather than under a roof, as in an open-air concert.

clue.text: Play tune by artist originally labelled 'unremarkable'

indicators.note: to play with letters is to move them about, so the tune word is rearranged
'originally' points to the opening letter of the word after it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the first letter of labelled

explanation.surface: A melody by an artist is first given the label of being dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play tune' sounds like performing music; play signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral can describe something without strong character or colour, bland and plain, hence unremarkable.

clue.text: State has endlessly dry area with dam in the middle

indicators.note: without their ends, the two words that follow each lose their last letter
the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter alone

blocks.note: arid means dry
a zone is an area
the middle letter of dam

explanation.surface: A US state contains a vast desert region with a dam at its centre, like the Hoover Dam.
explanation.walkthrough: Endlessly applies to both dry and area: ARI(D) and ZON(E), then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is one of the fifty United States, in the desert south-west, home of the Grand Canyon.

clue.text: Novel appears heartlessly mean about journalist

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the word after loses its central letters
'about' means moved around, so the letters gathered here are rearranged

blocks.note: novel means new
taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written; losing its heart leaves MN

explanation.surface: A cruel, stingy reporter features in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' wants to be the anagram signal, but it is NEW; heartlessly applies to mean, not appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaperman is someone who works for a newspaper, especially as a reporter or editor.
